html:
At Clontarf, just north of Dublin, on Good Friday 1014, the army of Brian Boru, High King of Ireland, defeated the King of Leinster and his allies, the Norse of Dublin and Viking fighters from overseas.

Brian had risen from a minor kingdom in Munster to claim rule over all Ireland. Leinster and Dublin revolted against him. His army won the battle, but Brian himself, too old to fight, was killed in his tent.

Later stories made Clontarf a national victory that drove the Vikings out of Ireland. In fact the Norse kept Dublin, which they had founded, and Irish kings went on fighting each other. But Brian's claim to be king of all Ireland became a model for later kings, until the Norman invasion.
sum: At Clontarf, just north of Dublin, on Good Friday 1014, the army of Brian Boru, High King of Ireland, defeated the King of Leinster and his allies, the Norse of Dublin and Viking fighters from overseas.
